data.name: Review a pull request
data.goal: Every pull request on harbor/ledger gets a first review before a person looks at it.
data.output: One review comment on the pull request. A pull request with nothing to flag gets a short approval note.

data.name: Cites file and line
data.statement: Every finding names the file and line it is about.

data.name: No style nits
data.statement: The review raises no formatting or naming point the linter already enforces.

data.name: Pull request opened or updated
data.condition: A pull request on harbor/ledger is opened or gets a new head commit.

data.instructions: Review the diff for correctness, missing tests and unclear names. Summarise the findings in one comment.
Review the diff for correctness and missing tests. Give every finding as path:line and the reason. Leave formatting and naming to the linter. Summarise the findings in one comment.
data.rationale: Four of six reviews under revision 1 gave findings without a file or line, so the author had to search for them.
data.decision_note: Matches how we review by hand. Activate.

data.name: Reproduce a reported bug
data.goal: A bug report comes with a script that shows it, before anyone works on a fix.
data.output: A comment on the issue with the script and the version it fails on, or a note that it does not reproduce.

data.name: Attaches a failing script
data.statement: The comment carries a script that fails on the reported version.

data.name: Names the version
data.statement: The comment names the exact version or commit it reproduced on.

data.name: Issue labelled bug
data.condition: An issue on harbor/ledger gets the bug label.

data.instructions: Check out the version the report names, write the smallest script that shows the bug and post it on the issue.
Check out the version the report names inside a fresh container, write the smallest script that shows the bug and post it on the issue with the container image.
data.rationale: Issue 89 did not reproduce because a cached build hid the bug.
data.decision_note: A container adds six minutes to every issue. A clean worktree already avoids the cached build; say so in the skill instead.

data.name: Triage the support inbox
data.goal: Every support email reaches the team that owns its product area within the hour.
data.output: Each new email labelled with its area and assigned. An hour with no new email leaves nothing.

data.name: Routes to the owner
data.statement: Each email goes to the team that owns the product area it is about.

data.instructions: Read the emails received since the last run. Label each with its product area and assign it to the owning team.

data.name: Judge finished runs
data.goal: Every finished run of a workflow with criteria is judged within a day.
data.output: One evaluation per run and criterion, on a branch for review. A day with nothing to judge leaves nothing.

data.instructions: List the runs to judge. For each, read its traces and outputs and record one evaluation per criterion.

data.name: Propose revisions from failed judgments
data.goal: Instructions that keep failing a criterion get a proposed fix, with the runs that show the problem.
data.output: At most one proposed revision per workflow, on a branch, citing the evaluations it answers.

data.instructions: For each workflow, read failures_to_answer and revision_history. Where one criterion fails repeatedly and no rejected revision already tried the fix, propose a revision and cite the evaluations.

data.name: Post the weekly agent report
data.goal: The team sees each week what its agents ran, what failed and what it cost.
data.output: One message in #eng-agents with runs by outcome, failures and cost by revision.

data.instructions: Read workflow_scorecard, failed_runs since the last report and revision_cost. Post them as one short message.
